# Claims and ethics

## Supported descriptions

- embodied whole-connectome neural model;
- connectome-constrained virtual fly;
- autonomous digital-organism experiment;
- 2D sensory world with a strict information boundary;
- full loaded graph combined with a disclosed VNC/body model.

## Unsupported descriptions

Do not describe the project as:

- a living biological fly;
- an uploaded individual;
- proof of consciousness or sentience;
- an exact reconstruction of the scanned animal;
- a complete brain-and-body emulation;
- evidence that the system believes it is alive.

## The strongest defensible statement

The neural model cannot access the browser, editor, observer, room coordinates or target positions. Its information about the chamber is produced through sensory and bodily signals, and its effects on the chamber occur through an explicit neural-to-VNC-to-body loop.

## Interpretive captions

The interface occasionally says that the fly is “walking”, “recalling” or “turning away”. These are observer-side interpretations of numerical state. They are generated after the causal update and never feed back into control.

## Welfare uncertainty

There is no accepted evidence that this class of simplified simulation has subjective experience. The project nevertheless keeps intervention logs and avoids asserting that uncertainty is settled in either direction.
